courses.title: Python Foundations
courses.summary: Write your first programs, then grow them into tested, organized projects.

units.title: Build Your Own Adventure
units.summary: Output, variables, input, and choices in one connected story.

lessons.title: Open the story
lessons.description: Give your adventure a setting and a surprise.

lessons.title: Create your hero
lessons.description: Give the adventure a hero and a useful tool.

lessons.title: Meet the player
lessons.description: Let someone else name the hero.

lessons.title: Choose a path
lessons.description: Make the story respond to a choice.

lessons.title: Launch your adventure
lessons.description: Bring a player, a setting, and a choice into one small game.

units.title: Numbers and decisions
units.summary: Arithmetic, whole numbers and decimals, numbers from input(), comparisons, Boolean logic and elif.

lessons.title: Count the treasure
lessons.description: Give your adventure a score, and share out a chest of coins.

lessons.title: Average the scores
lessons.description: Find the average of two riddle scores, decimals and all.

lessons.title: Score the riddle
lessons.description: Turn the player's replies into numbers, and keep score when a riddle is solved or missed.

lessons.title: Too high or too low?
lessons.description: Compare the player's guess with the riddle keeper's secret number.

lessons.title: Close enough?
lessons.description: Decide whether a guess is close or out of range by joining comparisons together.

lessons.title: The riddle keeper's verdict
lessons.description: Give points for a guess by how close it is, choosing exactly one branch.

units.title: Repeat and explore
units.summary: while and for loops that always finish, running totals, and loops inside loops.

lessons.title: Keep guessing
lessons.description: Let the player keep guessing the secret number until they get it right.

lessons.title: Three tries
lessons.description: Give the player three tries, and make sure the loop always ends.

lessons.title: Step by step
lessons.description: Count the steps of a staircase with a for loop and range(), two at a time.

lessons.title: Keep the score
lessons.description: Add up the points from every round of the riddle keeper's game, count the empty rounds, and find the average.

lessons.title: Rooms on the map
lessons.concept: Loops · a loop inside a loop
lessons.description: Walk the riddle keeper's map row by row, count the coins in each room, and add them all up.

units.title: Keep track of a world
units.summary: Lists, positions and slices, looping over a list, dictionaries, and sets.

lessons.title: Pack the bag
lessons.description: Pack the hero's bag one item at a time, count what is in it, and check whether something was packed.

lessons.title: First and last
lessons.description: Pick supplies out of the quartermaster's list by their position, and slice off the middle.

lessons.title: Market day
lessons.description: Go through every treasure in the list: add them up, keep the valuable ones, and find the biggest.

lessons.title: Rooms of the keep
lessons.description: Remember what is in every room of the keep, look a room up by its name, and cope with a room that is not there.

lessons.title: Rooms already visited
lessons.description: Keep track of the rooms two explorers have seen, with no repeats, and compare where they have been.

units.title: Organize your code
units.summary: Functions: defining and calling, parameters, return values, local names, and splitting a program into parts.

lessons.title: A scene you can replay
lessons.description: Name a scene once with def, then play it as often as the story needs.

lessons.title: Any hero, any place
lessons.concept: Functions · parameters, defaults and named arguments
lessons.description: Write one scene that works for every hero and place, with a mood that has a sensible default.

lessons.title: Score the guess
lessons.description: Have the riddle keeper's scoring hand its answer back, so the rest of the game can use it.

lessons.title: The purse that must change
lessons.description: Keep the hero's coins right by handing values in and back, instead of reaching outside a function.

lessons.title: Break the battle into parts
lessons.description: Adventure v2: split a fight into small functions that each do one job, and build the whole from them.

units.title: Recover and investigate
units.summary: Reading tracebacks, debugging step by step, try and except, raising your own errors, and asking until the reply is valid.

lessons.title: Read the crash report
lessons.description: The shop's ledger crashes. Read each crash report from the bottom up, and fix the line it points to.

lessons.title: Wrong by one
lessons.concept: Debugging · find the line that is wrong
lessons.description: A tally that never crashes but gives the wrong answers. Find its bugs by testing small cases and printing what is going on.

lessons.title: A safe share
lessons.description: Share the coins without crashing, whatever the player types.

lessons.title: Rules of the game
lessons.description: Make a function refuse a value that breaks the rules, with a message that says why.

lessons.title: Ask until it is right
lessons.concept: Input · asking again until the reply is valid
lessons.description: The bridge keeper keeps asking until the reply makes sense, and says what was wrong each time.

units.title: Libraries and modules
units.summary: Importing modules, random numbers with a seed, the math module, dates with datetime, and modules of your own. A local setup lesson comes later.

lessons.title: The toolbox
lessons.description: Borrow ready-made tools from Python's math module to measure the round tower.

lessons.title: The riddle keeper's dice
lessons.concept: random · seed, randint, choice and shuffle
lessons.description: Roll the riddle keeper's dice, and learn why a seed makes chance repeatable.

lessons.title: As the crow flies
lessons.concept: math · roots, rounding and nearly-equal numbers
lessons.description: Measure how far the treasure is in a straight line, and round the answers honestly.

lessons.title: A study schedule
lessons.description: Plan study sessions on real calendar dates, across month ends and leap days, and spot the weekends.

lessons.title: A helper file
lessons.description: Quiz tool v1: keep the grading rules in a file of their own, and use them from the main program.

units.title: Trust your changes
units.summary: Writing tests with assert, choosing test cases and boundary values, type hints, and refactoring safely.

lessons.title: Test the scorer
lessons.description: Write tests that prove the streak bonus works, and that catch it when it doesn't.

lessons.title: Choose good cases
lessons.concept: Testing · typical, edge and unusual cases
lessons.description: Pick the test cases a careless average() would trip on: empty lists, decimals, and the last score.

lessons.title: Edges of the rule
lessons.description: The ferry charges by age. Test right at the edges of each price, where off-by-one bugs hide.

lessons.title: Labels for values
lessons.concept: Type hints · saying what a function takes and gives
lessons.description: Label what goes into the coin-sharing function and what comes out, so anyone reading it knows how to use it.

lessons.title: Tidy without breaking
lessons.description: The shop's till works but repeats itself. Tidy it into a price list and one function, without changing a single line it prints.

units.title: Save and load
units.summary: Reading and writing text files, saving with JSON, tables in CSV files, and coping with missing or damaged data. A local setup lesson comes later.

lessons.title: The save file
lessons.concept: Files · open, read and write text
lessons.description: Read the scores the game saved, line by line, and write a summary file of your own.

lessons.title: Save the game
lessons.description: Load the hero's saved game, add what they found, and save it again, ready for next time.

lessons.title: The score table
lessons.concept: csv · tables in a text file
lessons.description: Read the tournament's results table, add up each team's points, and find the top player.

lessons.title: The damaged save
lessons.concept: Files · coping with missing and bad data
lessons.description: Load the game's settings even when the file is missing or damaged, and say what was skipped.

units.title: Patterns in text
units.summary: String methods and f-strings, searching with regular expressions, groups and replacing, and checking formats honestly.

lessons.title: Clean up the answers
lessons.description: Check the riddle keeper's answers fairly, whatever capitals and spaces the player types, and tidy them for display.

lessons.title: Spot the ticket code
lessons.description: Recognise ticket codes in the messages that come in, whether a whole message is one or it hides inside other text.

lessons.title: Read the message log
lessons.description: Pull the time and the speaker out of each message, then print the log again with every time hidden.

lessons.title: Check the form
lessons.concept: re · checking a shape, and its limits
lessons.description: Check usernames and times on the sign-up form: the right shape first, then values that make sense.

units.title: Model a larger program
units.summary: Classes and attributes, methods that change an object, objects built from other objects, and when a dictionary or a function does the job better.

lessons.title: Make a hero
lessons.description: Design a Hero blueprint once, then make a whole party of heroes from it.

lessons.title: Potions and blows
lessons.description: Give the hero actions of their own, and keep the rules for health and potions inside the class.

lessons.title: A hero with a pack
lessons.description: Build the hero from smaller parts: a pack with a weight limit, holding items, each class doing one job.

lessons.title: Not everything needs a class
lessons.description: Classes are a tool, not a rule. Learn to tell when a dictionary or a plain function does the job more simply.

units.title: Final project
units.summary: Plan, build, test, and explain a project of your own. Choosing and planning it opens first; building and reviewing it come next.

lessons.title: Choose your project
lessons.concept: Planning · a brief before the build
lessons.description: Pick your final project, from a word game to a full app, and plan it: who it is for, what it must do, and what waits.

courses.title: Hackathon Ready
courses.summary: Scope, build, and demo a small working project with a team, against the clock.

units.title: Idea to MVP
units.summary: Cut an idea down to a minimum viable product.

units.title: Time-boxing
units.summary: Plan in fixed time blocks and know what to drop.

units.title: Teamwork with Git branches
units.summary: Feature branches, small pull requests, and reviews.

units.title: Using public APIs safely
units.summary: Rate limits, terms of use, and keeping keys out of frontend code.

units.title: Quick UI prototyping
units.summary: From a paper sketch to a minimal working interface.

units.title: Demo and pitching
units.summary: A two-minute demo that shows what works.

units.title: Judging criteria
units.summary: How projects are judged, and assessing your own honestly.

courses.title: Git and GitHub Essentials
courses.summary: Track changes, work on branches, and open your first pull request.

courses.title: Web Foundations: HTML and CSS
courses.summary: Build an accessible, responsive personal website.

courses.title: JavaScript and the DOM
courses.summary: Make web pages interactive with events and state.

courses.title: Data and SQL
courses.summary: Ask questions of real tables with queries, joins, and constraints.

courses.title: Data Investigation with Python
courses.summary: Answer an original question with a documented dataset.

courses.title: Computer Science Foundations
courses.summary: Representation, searching, sorting, complexity, and recursion.

units.title: How data is stored
units.summary: Binary, hexadecimal colours, characters and bytes, and why decimals drift.

lessons.title: Lamps on the tower
lessons.description: The signal tower shows numbers with a row of lamps. Read them, and set them, in binary.

lessons.title: Colours on the flags
lessons.description: The tower signals with coloured flags, written as six hex digits. Turn them into amounts of red, green and blue, and back.

lessons.title: Coded messages
lessons.concept: Text · characters as numbers, and bytes
lessons.description: Messages leave the tower as numbers. Shift letters to make a simple code, and count the bytes a message really takes.

lessons.title: The ledger that would not balance
lessons.description: The tower ledger adds up prices. Find out why decimals drift, and keep money exact by counting cents.

units.title: Thinking in steps
units.summary: Pseudocode, tracing a program by hand, and what stays true in a loop.

units.title: Searching
units.summary: Linear search, binary search, and counting steps as lists grow.

lessons.title: Search the shelf
lessons.concept: Searching · one item at a time
lessons.description: The archive keeps records on long shelves. Search them one by one, and count how many you had to look at.

lessons.title: Halve the shelf
lessons.concept: Searching · binary search on a sorted list
lessons.description: When the archive is sorted, you can skip half of it with every look. Find records in a handful of steps.

lessons.title: How the work grows
lessons.concept: Searching · counting steps as lists grow
lessons.description: Compare the two searches by counting, not timing: how many looks does each need as the archive grows?

units.title: Sorting
units.summary: Selection sort, merge sort, and comparing them on real inputs.

units.title: Recursion
units.summary: Functions that call themselves, base cases, and when a loop is better.

units.title: Data structures
units.summary: Stacks and queues, hash tables, trees and graphs.

units.title: Your comparison
units.summary: Design an experiment comparing algorithms, and write it up.

courses.title: Node.js and APIs
courses.summary: Build an API with routes, validation, and a database.

courses.title: Full-Stack Builder
courses.summary: Ship a client, API, and database project with automated checks.

courses.title: Engineering Depth
courses.summary: Electives in C and memory, discrete foundations, numerical methods, and embedded simulation.

courses.title: TEST FIXTURE (never shown to learners)
courses.summary: Test data for hidden function calls.

units.title: TEST FIXTURE hidden calls
units.summary: Test data.

lessons.title: TEST FIXTURE triple
lessons.description: Test data.

fixture.u10.title: TEST FIXTURE triple
fixture.u10.question: Test data?
fixture.u10.challenge: Write triple(n), which returns n times 3.

errorHints.text: Use the value of n, not a fixed answer.

otherWays.code:
def triple(n):
    return n + n + n

response.feedback: Your program printed the expected output for all 2 test cases, including 1 hidden case. Read your code once more: could you explain each line to someone else?
Your function returned something different for another number you cannot see (a hidden test case).
